directAnswer: To restart your WiFi router, unplug it from the power source, wait for about 10 seconds, and then plug it back in.
summary: Restarting your WiFi router can help resolve connectivity issues and improve network performance.

sections.heading: Understanding the Restart Process
sections.body: Restarting your router clears temporary settings and connections, which can help fix issues like slow speeds or dropped connections.

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Restart Steps
sections.body: The steps to restart your router may vary slightly based on the model and manufacturer.

steps.title: Unplug the Router
steps.detail: Locate the power cord of your router and unplug it from the wall outlet.

steps.title: Wait
steps.detail: Wait for at least 10 seconds to ensure that all power is drained from the device.

steps.title: Plug it Back In
steps.detail: Reconnect the power cord to the router and wait for it to fully reboot, which may take a few minutes.

steps.title: Check Connectivity
steps.detail: Once the router's lights indicate it is operational, check your device for internet connectivity.

faqs.question: What if my router does not have a power switch?
faqs.answer: If your router does not have a power switch, simply unplugging it from the power source is the correct method to restart it.

faqs.question: How often should I restart my router?
faqs.answer: It's generally recommended to restart your router once a month or whenever you experience connectivity issues.

faqs.question: Will restarting my router delete my settings?
faqs.answer: No, restarting your router will not delete any settings. However, a factory reset will.

caveats: If your internet connection issues persist after restarting, consider checking with your Internet Service Provider.
